mutations.before: if (org === LOCAL_TENANT.orgId) throw new Error('org "local" can never be deleted.');
mutations.after: if (org === "never-local") throw new Error('org "local" can never be deleted.');
mutations.because: without the LOCAL_TENANT check the CLI would tombstone 'local'. The arguments test asserts --org local rejects with 'org "local" can never be deleted.', so expect(...).rejects.toThrow('org "local" can never be deleted.') fails on that assertion line.
command: org CLI refuses bad arguments and the local org before opening anything

mutations.after: const outcome = await requestOrgDeletion(db, { orgId: org, requestedBy: "cli" });

command: org CLI apply tombstones the org and queues one org row and purges nothing

mutations.before: return row.kind === "org" ? purgeOrg(db, orgId, row) : purgeCampaign(db, orgId, row);
mutations.after: return row.kind === "campaign" ? purgeOrg(db, orgId, row) : purgeCampaign(db, orgId, row);
mutations.because: the dispatch is inverted: an org row is sent to purgeCampaign (which rejects a non-uuid subject), and a campaign row is sent to purgeOrg (which rejects a live org). The purgeRow test asserts the exact error messages, so expect(...).rejects.toThrow(...) fails.
command: purgeRow sends an org row to purgeOrg and a campaign row to purgeCampaign

mutations.because: org rows are released as not-implemented instead of dispatched to purgeRow. The end-to-end sweep test asserts { purged: 2, failed: 0 } for the first sweep, so expect(first).toEqual({ purged: 2, failed: 0 }) fails when the org row is released as failed instead of retried.
command: sweep claims the org row and purges the org end to end

mutations.because: the log line names 'campaign' instead of the row's kind. The end-to-end test asserts the org row's log line contains 'retry', so expect(lines.some((l) => l.includes(`${orgRowId}: retry`))).toBe(true) fails when the line reads 'campaign <id>: retry'.
command: sweep claims the org row and purges the org end to end
